scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: When you log in, the website checks your password. But a well built site never actually stores it. How?

scenes.name: hash
scenes.text: Your password goes through a hash function. A one way math scramble that turns it into a fixed jumble of characters.

scenes.name: oneway
scenes.text: Same input always gives the same hash. But you can't run it backwards to get the password.

scenes.name: login
scenes.text: At login, what you type is hashed again. If the two hashes match, you're in, without the site ever seeing the original.

scenes.name: salt
scenes.text: Sites also add a random extra value, called salt, for each user. So two people with the same password get different hashes.

scenes.name: slow
scenes.text: Good systems use deliberately slow hashes, like bcrypt or Argon2, so guessing billions of passwords becomes painfully slow.

scenes.name: you
scenes.text: Still, use a different password on every site, and turn on two factor authentication. Leaks happen.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Hash, compare, salt, slow down. Your secret stays secret. Follow for more on how things really work.
